subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: Should an oversized or orphaned Codex native thread force a fresh-thread recovery before `chat.send` reports success, or should WebChat fail visibly before ACK when that recovery cannot be proven?
rationale: Current code has partial recovery paths, but choosing ACK semantics, forced native-thread rotation, and user-visible failure behavior is a product/runtime contract decision rather than a narrow mechanical repair.

options.title: Recover or fail before ACK
options.body: Make `chat.send` return success only after Gateway has proven dispatch can start against a usable Codex thread, force-rotating first when safe and failing visibly otherwise.

options.title: Keep non-blocking ACK with health recovery
options.body: Preserve immediate ACK semantics but add a visible blocked-run state, audit/health surfacing, and a one-session native-thread reset path.

options.title: Wait for live replay first
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a current-main fixture or live repro captures the exact orphaned-thread state.

recommendation.title: Recover or fail before ACK
recommendation.body: Make `chat.send` return success only after Gateway has proven dispatch can start against a usable Codex thread, force-rotating first when safe and failing visibly otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current native overflow rotation mitigation that any final contract would likely build on or revise.
